candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — postpartum breastfeeding education / positioning after cesarean birth
candidate.educational_objective: Teach a breastfeeding parent after cesarean birth that the football/clutch hold is one useful position for reducing pressure from the infant's weight on the abdominal incision.

options.A: Football or clutch hold, with the infant supported alongside the mother's body
options.B: Traditional cradle hold with the infant lying directly across the lower abdomen
options.C: Laid-back position with the infant's body resting directly over the incision
options.D: Stop breastfeeding until the abdominal incision has completely healed

candidate.rationale: AAP breastfeeding guidance identifies the football/clutch hold as particularly useful after cesarean delivery because it keeps the infant's weight off the abdominal incision. Other positions, including side-lying or well-supported alternatives, may also work depending on the parent and infant, so the item does not claim that football hold is the only acceptable position. In this specific scenario, however, it directly addresses pressure over the incision and is the best answer. B and C place more pressure over the abdomen, and cesarean birth is not a reason to stop breastfeeding. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The football/clutch breastfeeding position is particularly useful after cesarean delivery because it can keep the infant's weight off the abdominal incision.
